text.p: Austrian paper and cardboard maker Nettingsdorfer Beteiligungs AG said on Wednesday it expected 1997 pretax profit to rise as much as 15 percent mainly due to higher prices, erasing last year's drop.
"1997 will not become a spectacular year but I can imagine a rise in pretax profit by 10 to 15 percent," Nettingsdorfer's chief executive officer Heinz Kessler told a news conference.
"We do expect an uptick in prices by around 10 percent in the first half of the year," the group's chief financial officer Ulrich Stepski added.

In 1996, Nettingsdorfer, in which Ireland's Jefferson Smurfit Group Plc holds a 27.5 percent stake, posted a preliminary pretax profit of 187 million schillings, down from 368 million schillings. Sales fell to 3.6 billion after 4.3 billion schillings in 1995.
Nettingsdorfer said it would pay an unchanged dividend of four schillings.

In the medium term Nettingsdorfer would strive to produce 400,000 tonnes of paper a year, Kessler said. In 1996, the group's paper output rose three percent to 353,000 tonnes while disappointing paper prices caused a drop in sales to 1.9 billion schillings from 2.3 billion.
Pretax profit in the paper division fell to 89 million from 260 million schillings.
In the cardboard divison, Nettingsdorfer achieved stable output of 218,000 tonnes but sales slipped to 2.1 billion from 2.4 billion schillings. No further details were given.
Nettingsdorfer and Smurfit would strive to merge their Italian cardboard interests under a holding but little progress has been made up to now, Kessler admitted.
"We have made progress in terms of contents but there are still a lot of formalities which we have to solve", he said.
